relevance_note: This is a cohort-level clinical exome study of 1000 families in which TNFAIP3 is named only inside a group list of reclassified diagnoses ("TNFAIP3 (n = 1)"), with no identifiable person, no variant description and no HA20 diagnosis, so no individual-level TNFAIP3 data are reported.
method_note: Read only the paper, schema and rules; no script was used and no table was transcribed automatically. I searched the whole Markdown (including the Supplementary Material section, which contains only figure/table titles) for TNFAIP3, A20, haploinsufficiency and Behcet/HA20: the single TNFAIP3 mention is a count in a list of genes involved in upward reclassifications ('TNFAIP3 (n = 1)'). No case description, table row/column, pedigree, sex, age, variant string or clinical feature is attached to that person, and no HA20 or A20 haploinsufficiency diagnosis appears anywhere, so no person is identifiable (schema rule for reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant) and the individuals, variants, phenotypic_features and phenotype_checklist tables are empty. The 1505 participants (1000 probands, 505 relatives) and all other participants with variants in other genes are out of scope and are counted only in publications.cohort_size_as_stated; Table 1 is aggregate demographics with no per-person cells, so no stacked-cell (' / ') issue arose. n_patients_reported = 1 because the authors themselves state the count for TNFAIP3, even though no patient is described. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients was set to true on the strength of the statement that participants referred to this program 'were included in novel gene-disease associations for NCKAP1L (22) and PIK3CG (23)', i.e. some of its patients had been published earlier; this is an interpretation of that sentence rather than an explicit re-report statement, and reference (24), cited for the 22q duplication / IRF2BP2 re-evaluations, may also point to earlier descriptions of those participants. No contradictions between statements were found.

year.span: Journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology (2022)

study_type.span: A total of 1,505 individuals from 1,000 unrelated families were recruited from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Division of Intramural Research (DIR) between 2017–2019 to enroll onto a centralized sequencing protocol.

cites_prior_report_of_same_patients.span: participants originally recruited into other NIAID research protocols and subsequently referred to our program were included in novel gene-disease associations for NCKAP1L (22) and PIK3CG (23)
